stories.title: Trump admin approves potential Patriot missiles sale to Ukraine
summary: The Trump administration on Friday green-lit the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, the State Department said, but the Ukrainian president warned deliveries could take years.
The statement did not provide an estimate for when the weapons could be delivered to Ukraine.
The State Department said the weapons sale would be paid for with by donations from Ukraine’s allies but not with US funds.

stories.title: Over 1,460 illegal medical centres sealed in 3 months in KP
summary: PESHAWAR: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Healthcare Commission has sealed 1,465 illegal medical centres across the province during the last three months, according to its latest performance report on Friday.
According to the commission’s spokesperson, Azam Rehman, measures were also taken to improve the registration and licensing of healthcare facilities and address public complaints.
The report stated that 610 new medical centres were registered during the last three months, bringing the total number of registered healthcare facilities in the province to 22,910.

stories.title: CM Maryam launches Rs2 trillion PIVOT initiative to boost industry, exports
summary: LAHORE: Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Friday officially launched the Punjab Innovation for Value, Opportunity and Transformation (PIVOT) Plan 2026-29 – around Rs2 trillion economic strategy aimed at positioning Punjab as an export-led industrial hub.
Speaking at the launch, the chief minister said: “Punjab is ready to move towards a new model of economic growth, driven by industry, innovation, value addition and exports.

Fatima Group Chairman Fawad Mukhtar expressed confidence that the business community would fully support the initiative, lauding the chief minister’s thorough engagement and declared that this venture represents the economic future of both Punjab and Pakistan.

stories.title: Man sets himself ablaze outside court after daughter’s ‘rapist’ acquitted in Lahore
summary: LAHORE: A man set himself on fire outside the Muzaffargarh district courts on Friday, after an accused in the rape case of his daughter was acquitted after nine years of proceedings.
A court acquitted the rape case accused on Thursday for lack of evidence, nine years after the case was instituted.
The litigant said he had spent years pursuing the case and that his daughter had also been divorced by her husband because of rape.

stories.title: Man held in Karachi for swindling, blackmailing woman via matrimonial app
summary: KARACHI: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Friday claimed to have arrested a man for allegedly depriving a woman of approximately Rs4.45 million by making empty promises of marriage on a matrimonial app.
Man found shot dead A young man with an alleged criminal record was found shot dead in North Karachi on Friday, police and rescue services officials said.

Man killed as coach overturns A man was killed while five others were injured when a passenger coach overturned while avoiding a collision with a police mobile near Naval Colony gate in Baldia Town on Friday, police and rescue services officials said.

stories.title: Commuters risk life and limb as poles not removed from middle of road in Hyderabad
summary: HYDERABAD: Carpeting of a new road and opening it for traffic, despite many electricity poles still standing in the middle of the dual carriageway, has triggered a heated debate on social media as travelers risk life and limb.

Until now used to be known as Ghora Ground, the artery has been converted to an asphalt road, the landscape otherwise being an abandoned waterlogged area used for electricity transmission to Deh Fouj Gah through the poles.

He said proximity of Qasimabad grid station with the road necessitated relocation of electricity infrastructure, adding that until Wednesday (Oct 28), 97 poles had been shifted and the remaining ones would be relocated by Nov 10.

stories.title: SHC moved against construction on Karachi's Nehr-i-Khayyam
summary: KARACHI: The Jamaat-i-Islami, along with some Clifton residents, moved the Sindh High Court against the provincial government for carrying out construction and development activities on Nehr-i-Khayyam.

They asked the SHC to declare as illegal the alleged conversion, alteration or utilisation of the storm-water drain into a recreational park or commercial venture or any other inconsistent purpose without lawful authority and compliance with the applicable laws.
They urged the court to preserve Nehr-i-Khayyam for its lawful purpose and primary function as a storm-water drainage channel.

stories.title: The cost of injustice
summary: In her extraordinary book Weathering: The Extraordinary Stress of Ordinary Life in an Unjust Society, Dr Arline Geronimus has shown that the constant physical toll of coping with injustice can have deep physical and mental consequences.
One category of disadvantaged people in Pakistani society is women.
These figures can be attributed to the fact that women do not feel confident about their own or their children’s futures because they live in a society where injustice is common.

stories.title: Pakistan’s reforms deficit
summary: PAKISTAN has never suffered from a shortage of civil service reform proposals.
The latest reform package is significant not because Pakistan has rediscovered civil service reform, but because it attempts to address several structural weaknesses simultaneously.

The real reform is to build institutions where competence matters more than cadre, performance more than seniority, expertise more than connections and public service more than institutional privilege.

stories.title: Excessive punishment
summary: The judge held that Ms Mazari-Hazir and Mr Chattha had attempted to “compromise the security arrangements [made for the team] through pressuring security officials”.
Ms Mazari-Hazir is one of the most prominent champions of civil and human rights from the legal community, and has often taken cases involving some of Pakistan’s most vulnerable citizens pro bono.
The higher courts must hear their appeal swiftly, and the state must stop stretching antiterrorism laws to cover acts that bear no resemblance to terrorism.

stories.title: Smoke-emitting vehicles fined in Lahore
summary: LAHORE: During the current month in Lahore, as many as 1,763 smoke-emitting vehicles were fined, while a total penalty of Rs5.5 million was imposed.
During the same period, 739 vehicles were impounded and overloaded vehicles were offloaded in Lahore.
Furthermore, 2,018 industrial units were inspected across the Lahore division, resulting in 41 units and 146 restaurants being sealed for causing pollution.

stories.title: ANP announces MPC over Asghar Achakzai’s arrest
summary: QUETTA: Acting president of the Awami National Party (ANP), Balochistan, Jamaluddin Rishtya, strongly condemned the arrest of the party’s provincial president, Asghar Khan Achakzai, describing the charges against him as fake, baseless and fabricated.
He expressed growing concern among party workers and supporters, saying that the principles of justice and merit did not appear to have been upheld in Mr Achakzai’s case.
Highlighting Mr Achakzai’s political stature, Mr Rishtya said he had consistently worked to promote brotherhood, unity and harmony among different ethnic groups and tribes in Balochistan.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz forms body to review proposed LPG policy reforms
summary: The proposed reforms envisage allowing state-owned enterprises (SOEs) to enter the LPG import business and take over price-setting from the regulator, with prices subsequently passed on to the private sector.
Stakeholders said SOEs had limited LPG import experience and warned that the proposed levy on locally produced LPG would push prices higher, calling for a greater private-sector role.

A cabinet summary, seen by Dawn, proposes retaining monthly LPG pricing but removing Ogra’s role, with SOEs, including PSO, Sui companies, PARCO and Pakistan LNG, leading the shift to import-parity pricing.

stories.title: Barbs fly in Senate over rising poverty, PTI women’s detention
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Senate on Friday witnessed heated exchanges over rising poverty, the health and detention of PTI women leaders and activists, including Noreen Niazi, and an alleged increase in extrajudicial killings reaching Islamabad.
PTI Senator Azam Swati said he had spoken to Ms Niazi’s husband, who informed him that her treatment was progressing well. “He thanked the government for allowing her to meet her elder daughter.

The minister’s remarks that treatment would be determined by doctors rather than Ms Niazi’s wishes triggered protests and sloganeering by PTI members. “Let the House run, it will not work like this,” PPP Senator Shahadat Awan, who was presiding over the session, intervened.

stories.title: Qatari delegation arrives in Tehran for peace talks
summary: Iran retaliated with attacks on Israel and US assets, and has since blocked ships from using the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about a fifth of global oil consumption.
Separately, Iran said three oil tankers had been halted as they crossed the blockaded strait.
The gathering, held just days before the US midterm elections, also comes as global energy prices have soared since the US war on Iran began.

stories.title: KP police get tech to monitor counterterrorism operations
summary: PESHAWAR: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa police have integrated anti-drone systems and surveillance drones operating across the province into the Safe City Peshawar’s Command and Control Centre to strengthen security and surveillance capabilities.

Drones, anti-drone systems integrated into Peshawar’s Safe City network He said live monitoring of police operations, including those conducted by the CTD across the province, had also become possible, facilitating the timely sharing of information.

He said the integrated use of modern technology, drone surveillance, anti-drone systems and centralised monitoring would further strengthen the police’s operational capabilities, security surveillance and response to militant threats.

stories.title: Pakistan warns of Taliban repression as UN expert urges accountability
summary: WASHINGTON: Pakistan has warned that the Taliban continue to allow terrorist groups to operate from Afghan soil, as a UN human rights expert urged member states not to normalise relations with the Kabul regime without verifiable improvements in human rights.
Mr Ajmal said the deteriorating human rights situation reflected the Taliban’s continued disregard for their international obligations.

He cited the ninth Ministerial Conference on Women, hosted by Pakistan in Islamabad in July, at which the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation adopted the Islamabad Declaration, expressing concern that Taliban restrictions on women and girls were inconsistent with Islamic values.

stories.title: Four of a family found dead in Skardu home
summary: GILGIT: Four members of a family, including two young children, were killed by unidentified attackers near Madina Colony in Skardu, with police suspecting that the murders may have been motivated by so-called honour.
Police suspect ‘honour’ may be the motive behind killing of couple and their two young children Police said the family had no known enmity with anyone.

The GB inspector general of police (IGP) has directed the Baltistan regional police officer to conduct a thorough investigation, establish the motive behind the killings, identify the perpetrators and ensure their arrest.

stories.title: Bugti stresses collective efforts to combat terrorism
summary: QUETTA: Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti on Friday said the fight against terrorism was not the responsibility of any single institution but a collective struggle involving the state and society.

The chief minister said the provincial government was committed to equipping the police force with modern technology, quality training and a professional environment free from political interference and undue pressure.
CM Bugti said merit had been established as the guiding principle for appointments, transfers and the assignment of professional responsibilities within the police force.

stories.title: India’s animal centre vows reset after criticism
summary: This is Vantara: billed as the world’s biggest animal rescue centre, but also the target of persistent criticism over how it amassed an unprecedented collection, including critically endangered animals.
Vantara says it houses more than 150,000 animals from over 2,000 species, brought from 30 countries.
It urged reforms to ensure Vantara did “not inadvertently become a driver of illegal harvest of wild animals”.

stories.title: LHC orders abolition of ‘parchi’ system at hospitals
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court on Friday directed the Punjab government to ensure strict implementation of its commitment to abolish the “parchi” (slip) system in all public hospitals across the province within four weeks.
During Friday’s hearing, Special Secretary (Health) Nabila Irfan appeared before the court in place of the Specialised Healthcare and Medical Education Department provincial secretary.

Taking the undertaking on record, Justice Wains directed the authorities to ensure its strict implementation within four weeks and to submit a detailed compliance report, supported by documentary material, before the next hearing.

stories.title: Polio campaign launched in 97 high-risk districts across country
summary: ISLAMABAD: The third sub-national polio vaccination campaign of 2026, targeting 97 high-risk districts across the country, was launched on Friday.

Federal Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination Syed Mustafa Kamal inaugurated the campaign at the National Emergency Operations Centre for Polio Eradication, where he administered the first polio drops of the drive.
The Pakistan Polio Eradication Initiative (PEI) launched the campaign to protect approximately 24 million children from Nov 2 to 8 in 97 high-risk districts across the country.

stories.title: Govt urged to conduct forensic audit, probe into ‘irregularities’ in housing societies
summary: They said there are two major categories of issues in 41 cooperative housing societies: the first involved allottees who despite paying money were running from pillar to post to get possession of plots.
They said the basic objective behind establishing cooperative housing societies was to provide homes to ordinary citizens, working-class people, retired employees and overseas Pakistanis.

According to a probe of NAB Rawalpindi, housing schemes had sold 91,000 plots and files in excess of the available land or their approved layout plans (LoP) in twin cities of Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

stories.title: CDA directs removal of 'unauthorised' construction at JUI-F chief's residence in Islamabad
summary: The notice affixed outside the residence of the JUI-F chief — addressed to the legal owner of the property and dated Oct 30 (Friday) — highlighted three violations under the Islamabad Capital Territory Building Control Regulations 2020 (amended 2023).
The authority directed that the mentioned violations be removed within 15 days, starting Friday.
Meanwhile, after the notice was issued, Maulana Asjad Mahmood, the son of the JUI-F chief, claimed it was retaliation for pointing out alleged encroachments by a senior military official.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

stories.title: Pakistan seeks Saudi energy crisis support
summary: Pakistan has sought Saudi Arabia's support for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) supplies and invited investment in oil storage facilities and refinery upgrades as it grapples with supply disruptions linked to the Iran-US conflict and instability along key regional shipping routes.

The proposals were discussed at a meeting between Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervez Malik and Saudi Arabia's Ambassador to Pakistan Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy, according to a statement issued by the ministry.
He said strategic oil storage facilities in Pakistan would give Saudi Arabia greater flexibility in managing supply routes and reaching regional markets.

stories.title: PPP courts opposition for electoral reforms
summary: The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) on Friday intensified its efforts to secure opposition participation in the proposed parliamentary committee on electoral reforms as a party delegation met Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas to urge him to join the initiative.
The outreach came as the National Assembly approved the formation of a 30-member parliamentary committee to oversee electoral reforms.
Chaudhry said the committee was being formed to promote parliamentary consultation and consensus on improving the electoral system, ensuring transparency and introducing reforms.

stories.title: Singapore pushes deeper Pak trade ties
summary: Balakrishnan pushed for greater economic ties during his visit to Islamabad where he held talks with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and later met Chief of Defence Forces and Army Chief Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir.

The visit, the first by a Singaporean foreign minister since 2005, coincided with the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries and came months before Singapore assumes the chairmanship of ASEAN in 2027.

Prime Minister Shehbaz, meanwhile, accepted in principle an invitation from Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong to visit Singapore, providing another potential opening for high-level engagement between the two countries.

stories.title: FCC warns executive over ignored orders
summary: Amid an ongoing challenge regarding the non-implementation of superior courts' orders, the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has reminded the executive that compliance with a judicial decision is a constitutional requirement, not a matter of courtesy.
It also questioned whether the non-implementation of the order amounted to the contempt of court.
Interestingly, both the SC and the FCC are silent on the non-implementation of the judicial order in the military courts case.

stories.title: Ogra notifies 15.3pc increase in RLNG price for October
summary: According to the notification, RLNG’s sale price for SNGPL at the transmission stage increased by 13.9pc to $15.94 per mmBtu for October compared to $13.99 per mmBtu in September.
Meanwhile, RLNG sale price for SSGCL has been increased at the transmission stage by 15.25pc to $14.53 per mmBtu for October, against $12.611 per mmBtu in September.
The sale price at the distribution stage for the company thus also increased by 15.27pc to $16.396 per mmBtu for October compared to $14.22 in September.

stories.title: Pakistani three-wheelers go international as automotive manufacturer opens plant in Philippines
summary: In a post on the social media platform X, the Pakistan embassy in the Southeast Asian country said: “Pakistan-made three-wheelers have entered the Philippine market!” It said that Philippine President Ferdinand R.
Marcos Jr inaugurated the assembly plant of Pakistan’s Sazgar Engineering Works Limited.

He said that the plant was designed to assemble approximately 12,000 three-wheeled vehicles annually, covering both electric and internal combustion engines. “Sazgar has been building vehicles in Pakistan for over three decades.

stories.title: Hackers steal $6.3b from Binance
summary: Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a theft that analysts blamed on North Korea and said could be the largest financial heist of all time.

It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion, but Binance co-CEO Yi He said in a post on X that $3 billion represented only about 2% of the company's total user assets and public reserves.
Binance said it had set aside around $6.34 billion of company funds internally to cover the losses.

stories.title: Rifts mar G20 summit in Atlanta
summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged fellow G20 foreign ministers on Friday to work together for greater geopolitical stability and economic prosperity, warning that a series of crises posed serious threats to the global economic order.

But Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov's participation in the two-day gathering in Atlanta has roiled many G20 ministers, aggravating deep rifts over the wars in Ukraine and the Middle Eastthat experts and diplomats say could thwart real progress at the meeting.
Canada's foreign minister, Anita Anand, who has been critical of Lavrov's participation, missed the opening plenary session.

stories.title: Over 30 shops gutted as fire rips through furniture market in Karachi's Gulistan-i-Johar
summary: KARACHI: Over 30 shops were destroyed when a blaze erupted at a furniture market in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar in the early hours of Friday.
Rescue 1122 spokesperson Hassaan Ul Haseeb Khan said the fire erupted in a furniture market near Kamran Chowrangi.
In September, at least three people suffered minor injuries from smoke inhalation after a huge fire erupted in a factory at the Karachi EPZ, near Landhi Industrial Area.

stories.title: PPP delegation calls on Senate opposition leader, urges participation in proposed committee on electoral reforms
summary: On Friday, another PPP delegation, comprising the party’s secretary general Nayyar Bokhari, Senator Waqar Mehdi, Nadeem Afzal Chan and Rehman, visited Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas with yet another invitation to join the proposed body.

A day earlier, another PPP delegation invited Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai to participate in the parliamentary committee to promote consultation and discussion among parliamentary representatives on electoral reforms.
The PPP chairman had invited the opposition to join the Parliamentary electoral reforms process and “engage with the federal government”.

stories.title: NA adopts resolution stating workplace harassment not only sexual in nature, may manifest in gender discrimination
summary: ISLAMABAD: The National Assembly on Friday approved a resolution reaffirming that workplace harassment was not limited to conduct of a sexual nature but may also include intimidation, humiliation and gender-based discrimination.

It underscored that workplace harassment was not limited to conduct of a sexual nature, but “may also manifest through gender-based discrimination, intimidation, humiliation, degrading treatment, hostile behaviour and misuse of authority, whether sexual or non-sexual in nature”.

The resolution concluded by reaffirming that a workplace free from harassment, humiliation and gender-based discrimination was “not a privilege, but a fundamental requirement of human dignity, equality and justice”.

stories.title: ML-I phase one to cost $2.1b
summary: The government has informed the Senate that the first phase of the Mainline-I (ML-I) project would cost $2.1 billion, as Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif constituted a new committee to finalise funding plans for the second phase of the much-delayed scheme.
The Minister for Railways Hanif Abbasi informed the Senate on Friday that the estimated cost of the 480-kilometre Karachi-Rohri section is $2.1 billion.
The committee met this week to find ways to securitise Pakistan Railways' land to finance the project's second phase.

stories.title: Local businessmen demand level playing field
summary: As Punjab courts Chinese, Austrian and other foreign investors with long-term land leases and tax breaks, local businessmen are asking a simple question: will they get the same facilitation?
Punjab is not the only province that prefers foreign investors, all other provinces, including Islamabad, also want foreign investment as it brings dollars, transfer of technology and much more.
The Board of Investment says the government treats both local and foreign investors equally.

stories.title: FBR faces first tax shortfall of FY27
summary: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) collected Rs4.06 trillion in taxes during the first four months of the current fiscal year, facing a shortfall of Rs124 billion but clinging to hopes that it would receive a few more billions along with tax returns on Saturday.
Tax collection The FBR got Rs4.06 trillion in taxes during July-October of the current fiscal year, missing the target by Rs124 billion.
For the current fiscal year, the government and the IMF have given a Rs15.263 trillion annual tax target to the FBR.

stories.title: National Grid Co plans to issue Rs100b Sukuk
summary: It reviewed progress on capital market reforms, with particular emphasis on deepening Pakistan's corporate debt market, expanding the issuer and investor base, improving market infrastructure and facilitating access to long-term financing.
The council was informed that corporate debt issuances reached Rs291 billion during January-September 2026, following Rs326 billion raised in 2025, representing a 30% increase over 2024.
The market also witnessed 12 new listed corporate debt issuances worth Rs45.4 billion between February 2025 and September 2026, reflecting growing activity in Sukuk and other debt instruments.
